title: Set up an LLC
summary: Form an LLC: name check, Articles of Organization with a registered agent, a signed operating agreement, then the EIN, bank account, and state-tax registrations. The default for holding companies, agencies, and bootstrapped businesses — founders planning to raise priced venture rounds should incorporate a Delaware C-Corp instead, and an LLC that later takes that path runs the statutory conversion (see Convert an LLC to a C-Corp).

parts.title: Choose a formation service
parts.guidance: Choose the intended jurisdiction and entity form before comparing formation services. For a US LLC, compare filing assistance, registered-agent coverage, operating-agreement support, ongoing charges and tasks left to the founders. Once the founder responsible for formation approves the service, use its actual input requirements. A foreign entity option needs its own formation route and governing documents.

parts.title: Check name availability
parts.guidance: Search the relevant registry for the proposed name and check the entity suffix and restricted-word rules. Keep alternatives for the founders to choose and assess whether a reservation is useful. Domain and trademark checks address different questions. Use the selected name consistently in the filing; the registry ultimately decides whether to accept it.

parts.title: File Articles of Organization and appoint a registered agent
parts.guidance: Prepare the filing for the selected legal form and jurisdiction. For a US LLC, use the formation state’s current form with the chosen name, management details, address and required agent information. The organizer approves the final submission, fee and effective-date choice. Track acceptance or corrections. A non-US option requires its local procedure and a fresh applicability check of the following US steps.

options.title: Default — File Articles of Organization and appoint a registered agent
options.summary: File the selected state’s Articles of Organization or equivalent form using the approved name and management structure. Confirm the registered agent’s details and consent, and decide any available effective-date option before the organizer approves submission and fees. Track the application through registry acceptance and retain the issued formation record. Identify follow-up required by that state separately from services included in the formation package.

verify.how: The LLC appears in the Delaware entity search with a file number once the Certificate of Formation is stamped.

cost.note: Delaware domestic LLC Certificate of Formation filing fee.

options.title: India - LLP via MCA FiLLiP
options.summary: For an Indian LLP, resolve the partners, designated partners, registered office and business activity using the current MCA route. A local formation professional should verify the required documents and signatures before filing. The partners authorize the application and use the registry response to track acceptance or corrections. Plan the LLP agreement and tax setup separately; the Indian form does not inherit US LLC tax or governance treatment.
options.when: Forming the pass-through entity in India

options.title: UK - LLP at Companies House
options.summary: Prepare the UK LLP’s members, designated-member responsibilities, registered office, email and proposed LLP agreement. Use the current Companies House registration route, with submission approved by the authorized members. The certificate and registry record establish the registration outcome. Use the official LLP guidance for the subsequent UK accounting and tax work.
options.when: Forming the pass-through entity in the United Kingdom

references.title: Set up and run an LLP

options.title: Germany - UG (haftungsbeschraenkt)
options.summary: Give the German adviser or notary the founders’ identities, ownership, intended activity, office and capital proposal. Review the governing document and GmbHG section 5a capital and reserve rules before choosing the UG form. The founders execute the required local documents through the confirmed procedure. Track capital and registry requirements until registration, then use a German setup plan for subsequent work.
options.when: Forming the low-capital entity in Germany

options.title: France - SARL/EURL via INPI
options.summary: Prepare the chosen SARL or EURL’s owners, management, registered office, capitalization and required formation documents. Resolve the package with the formation adviser before the authorized applicant submits through the guichet unique. Respond to correction requests until the registry processes the filing. Use local governing and tax documents afterward; the remaining US LLC steps do not become applicable merely by selecting this option.
options.when: Forming the pass-through analog in France

parts.title: Receive the stamped Certificate of Formation
parts.guidance: Obtain the registry’s accepted formation record and check the legal name, entity number and filing or effective date. Resolve discrepancies with the filer before using those details for banking and tax setup. Save the issued document in the company records. A provider dashboard or payment receipt remains insufficient evidence that the registry accepted the formation.

parts.title: Draft the operating agreement
parts.guidance: For a US LLC, draft the members’ agreed contributions, ownership, management, voting, distributions, transfers and departure arrangements into the operating agreement. Highlight unresolved economics and management authority for the members to decide. Check the draft against the formation state and tax plan during legal review before execution. LLP, UG, SARL and EURL options require their appropriate governing documents.

parts.title: Members sign the operating agreement
parts.guidance: Reconcile the final US LLC agreement and schedules with the members’ actual ownership and contribution terms. Confirm the signers, capacities and effective date, resolve blanks, then circulate the approved version for execution. Keep signed counterparts together and track outstanding contributions separately. For a foreign entity, follow the local execution process for its governing document.

parts.title: Apply for an EIN
parts.guidance: Determine whether the formed entity needs a US EIN and whether one already exists. Use the accepted entity details and responsible-party information to select the appropriate IRS channel. The authorized representative reviews and submits the application, completing any third-party designation. Keep the issued confirmation for banking and tax records. A foreign formation option does not by itself establish a US EIN requirement.

verify.how: The EIN is issued in the XX-XXXXXXX format at the end of the online session — retain the CP 575 confirmation notice; banks and payroll providers ask for it.

cost.note: The IRS issues EINs for free; third-party services charge to file on your behalf.

parts.title: Open a business bank account
parts.guidance: Assemble the formation record, governing agreement, tax registration and signatory information requested by the selected bank. Submit identity documents only through its secure process. The designated applicant approves the account terms and application and completes identity checks. After approval, verify the legal account holder, authorized users and access arrangements. Any initial transfer needs its own payment approval.

verify.how: The dashboard shows account and routing numbers and a small inbound test transfer clears.

parts.title: Register for state taxes
parts.guidance: For a US LLC, assess employee locations, operations and sales for state tax accounts separately from foreign qualification. Use the tax adviser’s conclusions to set the account types and effective dates, then authorize the required filings. Capture agency confirmations and recurring obligations. A non-US formation route needs a local registration plan before any US state-tax step is treated as applicable.

verify.how: The state tax authority issues an account or registration number for each tax you registered.

metadata.supportReason: Formation services drive the state filing but expose limited APIs. The agent checks the name, drafts the operating agreement, and pre-fills every form; the state portal, the IRS EIN wizard, and member signatures stay manual.

geoNotes.summary: The Indian analog is the LLP: incorporated with the MCA via the FiLLiP form (mca.gov.in blocks automated checks — the government's NSWS portal fronts MCA services), with a partner-drafted LLP agreement filed within 30 days.
The pass-through analog is the LLP, registered at Companies House — though most UK founders just form a private limited company, since there is no US-style LLC and no check-the-box tax election.
geoNotes.actionLabel: Set up and run an LLP

geoNotes.summary: No LLC analog with pass-through: the low-capital route is the UG (haftungsbeschränkt) — a mini-GmbH formable from €1 with a notarized deed; the ministry's founders portal walks through the choices.
The closest analog is the SARL (or single-member EURL) — a simpler, statute-driven company than the SAS — formed like every French entity through the INPI guichet unique.

No LLC or check-the-box: the everyday small-company form is the Lda (sociedade por quotas), formable online through Empresa Online with quota capital from €1 — corporate tax treatment, not pass-through.

Canada has no LLC: corporations are the only limited-liability company form and there is no check-the-box pass-through election — the ULC (available in AB, BC and NS) is still taxed as a corporation in Canada and exists mainly for US tax planning.
